_comment: CTF-P1b — THE REGIONS OF AN AGENT HARBOR STORY, NAMING NO RENDERER'S LAYOUT.
Each region is one part of a story's drawing — the view, its frame's title
tab, the head and the rows of a panel or list, the active tab, the +N chip,
the '+' control, a hover popup, an open dropdown, a loading / empty / error
notice — and says which element it is in EACH renderer, in that renderer's
own terms: `web` is a CSS selector over the web views' classes (the first
visible match in document order, `document.querySelector`), `gpui` the
`data-ah-*` facts the GPUI views put on the element (every one present; a
non-empty value must match exactly). It is read by both capture paths and
transcribed into neither: `tools/visual-review/capture-storybook.mjs
--regions` (the browser's `getBoundingClientRect`) and `codetracer-gpui-story
--regions` (GPUI's own layout, read back through isonim-gpui's
`layout_bounds`). Where it is laid out is each renderer's own answer.
A region a story does not draw is absent from both sides' answer; a region
one side draws and the other does not is a failure of
`test_ctf_p1b_gpui_capture_matches_web_layout`, which compares the two
answers with PLAT-35's pane-rectangle comparator (`layout_questions
.compareAnswer`, `PaneRectangleTolerancePp`: 2 hundredths of the viewport
per edge, never raised).
A region marked `fill` is also checked for its BACKGROUND, which no layout
answer carries: the web capture records the colour the browser composites
behind the element (its own background over its ancestors'), and the layout
test reads the GPUI frame's pixel 4px in from the region's right edge, half
way down -- inside the element's padding, clear of its text -- against it.
